question: How many license plate readers mapped in the USA will be displayed by DeFlock.org on November 1, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Two readings put DeFlock at ~143.4k-143.9k around Oct 4-7, 2026: DeFlock.org's own counter (143,356, via Jalopnik Oct 4) and the deflocktheusa.com mirror (143,886, Oct 7). The mapped count grew explosively in 2025-26 (53k at end-2025, 135.8k on Aug 26), but adds slowed from ~500/day in Jul-Aug to ~190/day from late Aug to early Oct. Projecting 24 more days at a decelerating-to-steady rate gives ~+4-5k, so the median is ~148k. Downside: dedup cleanup (an HN commenter estimated a few % duplicates) or a stale counter. Upside: a renewed media-driven surge. Market check: none found on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or bookmakers.
calls.dossier:
- Resolves off the 'LPRs mapped in the USA' counter on deflock.org as accessed by Metaculus on/after Nov 1, 2026, not third-party mirrors or analyses.
- Event window: point-in-time reading on Nov 1, 2026. As of Now (Oct 8) about 24 days remain until then.
- Jalopnik, Oct 4, 2026: deflock.org shows 143,356 LPRs mapped in the country and 153 cities rejecting them.
- deflocktheusa.com/the-map (mirror, 'updated hourly'), Oct 7, 2026: 143,886 cameras across the US.
- LHS Magpie, Sep 25, 2026: 'more than 140,000' ALPRs mapped per DeFlock.
- RoadSigns.com analysis of DeFlock/OSM data, Aug 26, 2026: 135,844 total ALPRs (111,105 Flock). Year-end totals: 2023 = 432; 2024 = 4,344; 2025 = 53,119. About 20k in late Aug 2025.
- RoadSigns: Jul 17 -> Aug 26, 2026 added about 19,760 (about 500/day), during peak media attention to Flock.
- Implied Aug 26 -> Oct 4: about +7,500 in 39 days (about 190/day). Oct 4 -> Oct 7: about +530 (about 175/day), but this compares different sites.
- Hacker News 'Deflock hits 100k ALPRs Mapped in USA' (about June 2026). A commenter found about 2.5k duplicates, so a few % of the count, which is a cleanup risk.
- An older search snippet shows 83,743 on deflock.org (date unknown, likely spring 2026).
- Status quo: the counter keeps rising steadily. Deceleration is visible since August.
- Upside drivers: news cycles (city contract cancellations, Newsweek coverage) driving volunteer surges. Downside: dedup purges, the counter not refreshing, or counting-method changes.
- Searched but not found: the exact refresh cadence of the deflock.org counter, and any Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi market (none found).
calls.reference_class: Recent daily growth of the DeFlock/OSM ALPR count (Aug 26 -> Oct 7, 2026 window, ~190/day) extrapolated over a same-length remaining horizon

calls.reasoning: US-tagged ALPRs in OSM (DeFlock's source): ~113.9k Jul 11, ~116k Jul 17, 127.9k Aug 9, 135.8k Aug 26, ~142k Sep 24, 143,886 Oct 7 (deflocktheusa mirror). Growth of 400-500/day in Jul-Aug slowed to ~210/day late Aug-Sep and ~150-190/day recently (Michigan +215/-77 over 30 days implies ~190/day nationally). Projecting 24 days at a decelerated rate gives ~148-149k. Width covers rate uncertainty and possible counter differences or lag on deflock.org itself, which I could not read directly. No human market found on Polymarket or Manifold (harness search); Kalshi and bookmakers were not searched separately. Leaving the 130k-220k range would need a counter failure or an implausible jump, so no escape mass.
calls.dossier:
- Resolution: the number of LPRs DeFlock.org displays as 'mapped in the USA' when Metaculus checks on or after 2026-11-01. It resolves off DeFlock's homepage counter, not the mirror sites or global OSM totals.
- Counter mechanics (GitHub FoggedLens/deflock README): an AWS Lambda 'alpr_counts' queries Overpass for all ALPRs and US ALPRs and writes a JSON to S3. The count is OSM-derived and could lag if the job is stale.
- Event window: the snapshot is taken at or after 2026-11-01. As of 2026-10-08 there are about 24 days left; the count is a single level at that time.
- Data points (US): truth11 page dated 2026-07-11 quoting deflock.org: 113,899 'LPRs mapped in the USA'. NaturalNews 2026-07-22: >117,000. Fox News 2026-07-30: about 119,000. 127,878 on 2026-08-09 (US OSM, figure from a web-search summary of the stateofsurveillance.org guide). roadsigns.com: 135,844 on 2026-08-26, with net +19,760 from Jul 17 to Aug 26 (~500/day) and 16,348 additions in July (largest months in the dataset). mapatlas.eu: ~142,000 US (153,754 worldwide) on 2026-09-24. deflocktheusa.com/the-map: 143,886 on 2026-10-07.
- Implied net rates: Jul-Aug ~400-500/day; Aug 26 to Sep 24 ~210/day; Sep 24 to Oct 7 ~150/day (the Sep 24 figure is approximate).
- deflocktheusa Michigan page 2026-10-07: 3,694 cameras, 215 added and 77 removed in the last 30 days (net ~3.9%/month; scaled nationally ~5.5k/month, ~185/day).
- History: end-2023 432, end-2024 4,344, end-2025 53,119 (roadsigns.com). Growth in 2025-26 was rapid; recent months show deceleration.
- Status quo: continued net additions at a decelerated rate. Upside candidate: renewed media attention (AJC Sep 2026, SFist DeFlock SF Sep 2026) or mapping campaigns. Downside candidate: saturation of findable Flock cameras, cleanup or removals, or a stale counter.
- Mirrors and different filters (Flock-only vs all ALPR, US vs world) give numbers several thousand apart.
- Searched but not found: a direct read of the deflock.org counter today (the page is JS-rendered); a daily time series; any prediction market (none on Polymarket or Manifold per harness search; Kalshi and bookmakers not separately searched).
calls.reference_class: Recent net growth of the US OSM surveillance:type=ALPR count over 2-6 week windows during Jul-Oct 2026, extrapolated over the 24-day remaining horizon

calls.reasoning: DeFlock-derived US tallies: 142,848 (late Sep 2026) and 143,886 (Oct 7, deflocktheusa). OSM worldwide surveillance:type=ALPR: 153,754 (Sep 24) -> 155,639 (Oct 8, taginfo), so recent growth is ~100-150/day, down from ~350-400/day in Jun-Aug. With 24 days left, simple continuation gives ~146-147k; a return to the summer pace gives ~154k. I added spread because DeFlock's own homepage counter (not fetched) may differ from the derived tallies. Escaping below 130k needs a counter failure or redefinition (e.g. Flock-only, ~115k), priced at 3%. Escaping above 220k is implausible because DeFlock says it won't import the leaked Flock data. Market check: no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or bookmaker market found.
calls.dossier:
- Resolves off the 'LPRs mapped in the USA' figure shown on deflock.org when Metaculus accesses it on/after 2026-11-01. It does not resolve off deflocktheusa.com, raw OSM counts, or leaked Flock datasets. The deflock.org counter itself could not be fetched in this run (JS/API-served).
- Event window: point-in-time reading at/after 2026-11-01. As of 2026-10-08 there are about 24 days to go.
- Status quo: the count only grows through volunteer OSM edits. There are no bulk imports.
- deflocktheusa.com (DeFlock-sourced data): 143,886 US Flock+ALPR cameras as of 2026-10-07. Its late-Sep 2026 article: 142,848 active (115,062 Flock-brand), plus 10,179 documented-but-removed.
- OSM taginfo surveillance:type=ALPR worldwide: 155,639 (data 2026-10-08), with ~155,475 nodes.
- mapatlas.eu OSM worldwide counts: 71,644 (2026-01-01), 101,562 (2026-05-01), 153,754 (2026-09-24). US ~142k on Sep 24 (~92% of the total).
- Sep 24 -> Oct 8 worldwide gain was ~1.9k (~135/day). deflocktheusa late Sep -> Oct 7 gain was ~1k (~100/day).
- Earlier growth: 'DeFlock hits 100k ALPRs mapped in USA' (HN, ~early June 2026); 117,000 US (Washington Informer, 2026-07-22). That is ~11-12k/month in summer, versus ~3-4.5k/month implied in late Sep/early Oct.
- Jan-May 2026 worldwide rate: ~7.5k/month.
- An older snapshot of the deflock.org homepage counter read 83,743 (undated, likely early-mid 2026). The counter may lag or differ from other tallies.
- Upside regime-break candidate: in late Sep 2026 a researcher's leaked Flock dataset (~300k devices, ~123.6k cameras) went public with a takedown fight and media attention, which could drive volunteer mapping. deflocktheusa says DeFlock will not merge the leaked data.
- Downside regime-break candidate: a counter outage or definition change (e.g. Flock-only ~115k) or cleanup of removed cameras.
- Markets: none found on Polymarket or Manifold (harness search).
- Searched but not found: the live deflock.org counter value, an archived history of the counter, and a reliable daily OSM chronology after Aug 25 (API output was truncated).
calls.reference_class: Daily net growth of OSM/DeFlock US ALPR node counts over 2026 (Jan-Oct), extrapolated over a 24-day window

calls.reasoning: DeFlock.org's own counter read 143,356 on Oct 4 (Jalopnik); the deflocktheusa mirror read 143,886 on Oct 7. Net additions slowed from ~500/day (Jul-Aug) to ~210/day (late Aug-Sep) and ~100-190/day now. 27 days at that rate gives +3-5k, so the median is ~147.3k. The upper tail covers a renewed media-driven mapping surge (e.g. after the leaked Flock dataset). The 2% below-range mass covers a counter outage or redefinition. Market check: none found on Polymarket or Manifold (harness search); Kalshi and bookmakers not checked on this no-web run.
calls.reconciliation: The runs agree on the facts: deflock.org counter 143,356 on Oct 4, mirror 143,886 on Oct 7, and deceleration to ~100-190/day. The remaining disputes are about the current rate (Run 3's 100-150/day vs Runs 1-2's 150-190/day) and how much tail width to allow. I could not check these with no web access. Both the taginfo worldwide gain (~135/day Sep 24-Oct 8) and the mirror gain (~100/day late Sep-Oct 7) point to ~120-170/day, which puts my median slightly below Runs 1-2. I kept Run 3's reference class and a small low-side escape for counter failure, and narrowed the upper tail a little because the deceleration trend is consistent across sources.

disagreements.verdict: Can't settle without web access. The taginfo and mirror figures lean ~120-170/day; I used ~150/day as the central rate.

disagreements.claim: Whether deflock.org's counter differs materially from the mirrors
disagreements.verdict: Partly settled: the Jalopnik Oct 4 deflock.org figure is consistent with the mirror's Oct 7 figure at the current rate, so the gap is small.
Small (2%), for a counter outage or a Flock-only redefinition.
